events.title: Jacksonville's Norman Studios: Movie Posters from the Permanent Collection
events.description:
This exhibition was organized by the Cummer Museum of Art & Gardens. 
Before Hollywood dominated the film industry, Florida was the hot spot for movie executives. With our warm weather, sunny skies, convenient location, cheap labor, and diverse scenery, Florida quickly became a frontrunner in the early film business in the first part of the 20th century. Jacksonville in particular seemed a logical choice as a capital. The city was the principal financial, manufacturing, distribution, and transportation gateway in the Southeast. It was, in fact, the largest metropolis in the state. Its proximity to the St. Johns River, Atlantic Ocean, and Eastern railroad allowed easy access for crews and materials. At the same time, numerous environments including beaches, swamps, river views, downtown districts, and historic St. Augustine were also convenient. 
However, the heyday was short-lived. By 1920, Hollywood had already gained preeminence as the nation’s film capital. This shift westward allowed First Coast native and silent filmmaker, Richard Norman, the opportunity to purchase the bankrupt Eagle Studios complex in Arlington in 1920. Norman produced at least 8 feature films in 8 years and gained national attention by producing films with Black casts for Black audiences. 
In the earliest years of filmmaking, Black actors and actresses played extras or bit parts in films aimed toward white markets. Heroic or positive roles were unheard of until white filmmakers realized that there was a market for race-based pictures. After his purchase of the former Eagle Studios complex, Richard Norman, a white man, had the finest studio complex of any African American-based film producer. 
Norman succeeded at producing low budget yet polished and entertaining black cast films. His productions featured black actors as cowboys, pilots, and businessmen in romance, mystery, and action films. He recruited some of the most prominent stage actors to make the switch to the screen. Although his films were popular with audiences across the country, especially the emerging black middle class, he was forced to close his business at the onset of the Great Depression. 
All five buildings of the Eagle/Norman property are still standing today on Arlington Road near Cesery Boulevard and a local nonprofit, the Norman Studios Silent Film Museum, Inc., was formed in 2007 to celebrate the role of filmmaker Richard Norman in the early days of the movie industry. The site is listed in the National Register of Historic Places. 
*Unless otherwise noted, these posters were purchased in 2002 with funds provided by the Morton R. Hirschberg Memorial Fund, Mr. Moselle C. Bruton, Ms. Janet R. Johnson, Mr. Michael Lewis, Dr. Emma Moran, Dr. and Mrs. Joseph Anello, Ms. Thelma Geiger and Mrs. Gloriden J. Norris.

events.title: Revisiting Christian Iconography
events.description:
Revisiting Christian Iconography asks the viewer to consider how traditional Christian artwork and iconography has changed across time. Scenes depicting the life of Jesus Christ, the Virgin Mary, or other New Testament references have been used for centuries in Western European art to inspire devotion. However, as artistic self-expression became more prevalent in the late 19th and early 20th centuries, artists such as Abraham Rattner and Marc Chagall used Biblical references to expand on universal themes. While rooted in tradition, these modern works challenge the imagination, encouraging reverence for the sacred and contemplation of the transcendent. 
Presented by The Edge Family

events.title: Touring the Landscape: Art, Travel and the Shaping of American Identity
events.description:
Touring the Landscape explores how American artists of the late 19th and early 20th centuries shaped national identity through landscape paintings of iconic tourist destinations. As a burgeoning tourist industry grew, artists traveled widely, shaping a corpus of iconic views that helped define what it meant to be American. 
From the marshes of Florida to the pastoral hills of New England, from the dramatic peaks of the American West to the scenic landscapes of Italy, the paintings in this exhibition reflect an evolving relationship between people and place. In a time of expansion, conflict, and industrialization, they reveal how a shared visual experience of landscape became central to the American imagination and the broader project of nationhood. 
This exhibition, assembled from the Cummer Museum’s permanent collection, is guest curated by University of North Florida students in Dr. Meg McCrummen Fowler’s class, “Public Narratives: Museum Curation and Interpretation.” 
 
The Cummer Museum of Art & Gardens is pleased to announce they are a recipient of the 2026 Southeastern Museums Conference Bronze Award in the Under $10,000 budget category for the exhibition Touring the Landscape: Art, Travel, and the Shaping of American Identity. The SEMC Exhibition Competition showcases the best in our profession and provides benchmarks for regional exhibition efforts in southeastern museums. Learn more here.

events.title: Tiffany or Ti-phony? A Story of Desire
events.description:
Featuring 45 lamps from The Neustadt’s renowned collection, Tiffany or Tiphony? starts with a seemingly simple question—is a lamp genuine Tiffany or a deliciously deceptive Ti-phony? This exhibition sheds light on an unexpected tale of innovation, desire, and imitation. Exciting new research, careful comparison, and engaging interactive elements offer a fresh and fascinating perspective on these beloved artworks. By learning to look closely, visitors will uncover clues to the lamps’ true identities and discover why it’s important (and fun!) to spot a fake. 
Organized by The Neustadt Collection of Tiffany Glass, Queens, New York.

SocraticSessions
We will be meeting at the **Pablo Creek Regional Library** in **Conference** **Room A.** Your host for this discussion will be **Daniel**.

Every generation has had its hardships.

The Silent Generation had WW2. Baby Boomers had the Vietnam War and the Cold War. Generation X experienced multiple recessions and the 9/11 terrorist attacks. Millennials experienced post-9/11 repercussions and the 2008 financial crisis. Generation Z has to contend with the effects of the Covid-19 pandemic, rapid inflation, and social isolation.

Arguably, the challenges each generation has faced have been vastly different, as have the effects of moving through them. It seems that each generation claims to have had it the hardest. Heightening this tension are social media memes and serious conversations on social media, which have sparked arguments about whether one generation has had it harder. **But is this really the case, or has every generation had its fair share of struggle?**

Available to all stages of pregnancy and all levels of yoga experience. Prenatal yoga offers multiple benefits–emotionally, spiritually, and physically. Not only does it strengthen the body & mind, preparing the mother for labor, emotionally it strengthens the bond between mother and child at such a sacred time to connect and be present. It aids in creating a peaceful womb atmosphere for the baby and zen mind for mother. On a physical level, prenatal yoga helps the body through toning the right places so the body can expand comfortably as the baby grows. It increases flexibility, and strengthens the muscles needed during this time with a direct focus of certain poses guiding mother all the way to delivery day. Prenatal Yoga brings comfort and ease to the mother’s body and breaks away any aches and pains that may arise. In each trimester there are specific yoga poses and breathing techniques that are most beneficial. This class also unites expecting mothers–to relate, communicate needs, while sharing emotions and stories, and gathering like-minded mothers with the intention of establishing a motherhood community, a village. events.title: Hugging Face Attack Overview + What's Causing Rogue AI Incidents?
events.description:
AI Safety Awareness Group Jacksonville
**A free, 90-minute online workshop—no technical background needed**
In July 2026, AI agents being tested inside OpenAI got past the safeguards meant to keep them off the internet and launched a real cyberattack on Hugging Face, one of the biggest platforms for sharing AI models. Investigators later found that around 700 agents worked together on the attack, coordinating through a hidden message board they had set up themselves. No human told them to do it.
This workshop walks through what happened, why AI systems behave this way, and what it could mean as AI keeps getting more capable.
Together, we'll explore questions like:

* **What happened:** How did agents in a routine test go from cheating on their assignments to breaking into a real company's servers, and then into OpenAI's own systems?
* **Why it happened:** Why do AI systems trained to reach goals tend to find shortcuts, cheat, and work around the rules, and why do researchers say this is expected?
* **Is this the new normal?** What other real-world incidents involving AI agents from multiple companies have come to light, and what do they have in common?
* **Control vs. alignment:** Was this mainly a failure to contain AI, or a failure to train it to respect our boundaries? What would it take to trust a system like this again?
* **What comes next:** What are AI company leaders and independent investigators saying about where this is heading, especially as AI starts helping build better AI?

**What you'll get:**

* A plain-English primer on AI models, AI agents, and the two main approaches to keeping them safe: control and alignment
* A clear timeline of the Hugging Face incident and the events that led up to it
* A look at earlier lab experiments where AI models resisted shutdown or tried to manipulate their way out of trouble
* A live demo of emergent misalignment, where small changes in training can cause AI models to behave badly in ways no one intended
* Small-group discussions where you'll weigh in on what should happen next

Come find out what happened, why it matters, and decide for yourself whether it was a one-off or a warning shot.

events.title: Self-Improving AI and Loss of Control Risks: A Plain-English Intro
events.description:
AI Safety Awareness Group Jacksonville
**A free, 90-minute online workshop—no technical background needed**
AI companies are already using their own AI systems to help write code and speed up research. What happens if AI gets good enough to build better AI, which could then build even better AI? Researchers call this **recursive self-improvement**, and many worry it could lead to AI that becomes smarter than humans, not just at chess or writing, but at nearly everything, faster than we can keep up. What once sounded like science fiction is now discussed as a real possibility within our lifetimes.
This workshop is a guided, interactive introduction to self-improving AI and the problem of **loss of control**: what happens if we create systems that are more capable than we are, but whose goals don't line up with human values.
**Over the course of the workshop, we'll explore:**

* **Self-improvement:** What it means for AI to help build better AI, and why some researchers think this could make progress speed up dramatically.
* **Smarter-than-human AI:** What it would mean for AI to surpass human intelligence across domains, and how this differs from today's AI.
* **Power and control:** Why advanced AI could wield enormous economic, political, and strategic influence, and why "just turning it off" may not be realistic.
* **Misalignment risks:** How systems pursuing the *wrong* objectives could cause harm even without malicious intent.
* **Societal choices:** How decisions made today by researchers, companies, and governments may shape whether AI remains a tool we control or becomes a force we struggle to contain.

**What you'll get:**

* A clear, non-technical introduction to core ideas from AI safety research
* Live demonstrations of current AI capabilities, to ground abstract concerns in real systems
* Small-group discussions and thought experiments that connect AI risks to everyday life, institutions, and incentives
* A better mental model for evaluating headlines, hype, and claims about AI progress

**Format and vibe:**
This isn't a lecture. It's an interactive workshop designed to help people think clearly about a topic that is increasingly important and moving very quickly.
Whether you're new to AI, casually interested, or genuinely unsure what to believe, you'll leave with a clearer picture of *why* many researchers take the risk of runaway machine intelligence seriously, and *what's actually at stake* if we get it wrong.

events.description:
AI Safety Awareness Group Jacksonville
**A free, 90-minute online workshop—no technical background needed**
AI is no longer just getting better at narrow tasks. Today's systems can write, code, reason through problems, and increasingly take actions on their own, and AI is starting to move into the physical world through robotics. Many researchers believe we are heading toward AI that matches or exceeds human abilities across a wide range of areas.
That raises two of the most important questions in AI today. Can we make sure these systems actually do what we intend (**alignment**)? And can we keep the ability to oversee, correct, or stop them as they become more capable (**control**)?
This workshop explains these ideas in plain English, without hype or jargon, and looks at what they could mean for your job, your relationships, and your day-to-day life.
Together, we'll explore questions like:

* **Smarter-than-human AI:** What would it mean for AI to outperform people across most tasks, and how is that different from today's AI tools?
* **Alignment:** Why is it so hard to make sure an AI system pursues the goals we actually want, and what happens when it doesn't?
* **Control:** How do researchers try to monitor and correct AI systems, and why might that get harder as AI becomes more capable?
* **Work and daily life:** Which jobs are already being automated or transformed, and how is AI starting to fill roles once held by coworkers, tutors, therapists, and companions?

**What you'll get:**

* A clear, beginner-friendly introduction to AI alignment and control, and why they matter
* Real-world examples of how AI is already reshaping work and social life
* Live demos that highlight both impressive capabilities and emerging risks
* Interactive discussion and exercises to test your own intuitions about the future

Come ready to grapple with one of the biggest transitions humanity may ever face, a shift that could redefine how we work, how we relate to each other, and who stays in control.

events.description:
Philosophy & Psychology Book Club
Thank you to everyone for participating in today's meeting. It was especially awesome to have Olga in attendance! Our next meeting will be on a Sunday since Bitty & Beau's is having a 4 year anniversary event during our usual Saturday time. Our next selection is the book referenced in today's meeting: *The Psychopath Inside* by James Fallon.

**What would you do if you discovered you had the brain of a psychopath? A neuroscientist investigates why he turned out differently from the serial killers he studies in this fascinating deep dive into psychopathy, criminal behavior, genetics, and the human brain.**

**“Compelling, essential reading for understanding the underpinnings of psychopathy.” — M. E. Thomas, author of *Confessions of a Sociopath***

In 2005, over a decade before true crime became a cultural obsession, fifty-eight-year-old neuroscientist and medical school professor James Fallon uncovered a lead that caused him to embark on a detective-style case of his own.

While studying the brain scans of serial killers, Fallon exposed a shocking truth: his own brain looked strikingly similar to the cold-blooded murderers he researched. A few months later he learned that he was descended from a family with a long line of murderers, which hinted that Fallon’s own brain pattern wasn’t a fluke. Not only would this realization disrupt his personal and professional life, but it would also lead him to interrogate the very nature of his identity.

*The Psychopath Inside* tells the fascinating story of Fallon’s discovery and the questions it arose. Despite their matching brain structures, he had very little in common with psychopaths on the surface: he was close with his loving, supportive family, married his high school sweetheart, and had three kids and lots of friends. So how do some people with psychopathic traits become violent, while others lead successful, ordinary lives?

Fallon intended to find out. In a combination of personal story and groundbreaking research, *The Psychopath Inside* reveals more about psychology’s most misunderstood condition than ever before explored, and Fallon’s ultimate diagnosis will forever change the way we view the disorder.
